meal.reasoning:
The image clearly depicts a tuna mayonnaise sandwich—triangular white bread sandwich with visible tuna–mayo filling. I estimate this to be one half of a standard sandwich (approx. 140 g). Typical nutritional values for a whole tuna mayo sandwich vary:
• MyNetDiary lists ~295 kcal for 138 g sandwich with 17 g protein, 8.8 g fat, 39 g carbs, 4 g fiber, 4 g sugar, 428 mg sodium ([mynetdiary.com](https://www.mynetdiary.com/food/calories-in-tuna-mayo-sandwich-sandwich-29918254-0.html?utm_source=openai)).
• OpenNutrition reports for 150 g serving: 336 kcal, 19 g protein, 17 g fat, 27 g carbs, 3 g fiber, 4 g sugar, 592 mg sodium, plus cholesterol, vitamins and minerals ([opennutrition.app](https://www.opennutrition.app/search/tuna-salad-sandwich-Grg5Py3ibMVi?utm_source=openai)).
Given the appearance, a basic tuna–mayo without extra veggies, I lean toward the MyNetDiary data. Since the photo shows roughly half a sandwich (~70 g), I scale nutrients by 0.5.
Thus estimated values:
Calories ~148 kcal, Carbs ~19.5 g, Protein ~8.5 g, Fat ~4.4 g, Fiber ~2 g, Sugars ~2 g, Sodium ~214 mg. Other micronutrients (saturated fat, cholesterol, potassium, vitamins) are less certain; OpenNutrition gives some values per whole sandwich (150 g): saturated fat 3 g, cholesterol 28 mg, potassium 235 mg, calcium 145 mg, iron 3 mg, vitamin D 11 µg ([opennutrition.app](https://www.opennutrition.app/search/tuna-salad-sandwich-Grg5Py3ibMVi?utm_source=openai)). Scaling by half yields saturated fat ~1.5 g, cholesterol ~14 mg, potassium ~117 mg, calcium ~72 mg, iron ~1.5 mg, vitamin D ~5.5 µg.
Confidence: moderate. Visual estimation of portion is approximate; nutrient variability by mayo amount and bread type.
